done.why: I had seen a fair amount and hit a puzzle (the unicorn's key) with no obvious next step, so I stopped early.

about: A small Zork-style cave world with a barrow, a cavern, a formal garden and a gazebo. A forgetful Wizard keeps casting illusions, such as a basilisk and a unicorn, that the world admits are not real. A real unicorn wears a gold key.

moments.note: A basilisk appeared right after the Wizard's spell.
Attacking it told me it was an illusion, and the room was embarrassed about it. That was funny.
I walked into the dark with no warning and had to guess that I should turn on the lantern.
The unicorn vanished when I petted it, then came back later.
'Look at the unicorn's neck' failed, but 'examine unicorn' worked.
The ribbon is tied to be untied by somebody in particular. That is a nice hook.

wished: Find out who the unicorn's key is meant for.
Get a hint about what the glowing sword was warning me of.
Be able to use the matchbook.

lines.line: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: It set the playful tone and showed me what the Wizard does.

lines.line: The ribbon is tied in the sort of bow that is meant to be untied by somebody in particular
lines.why: It hints at a puzzle in a charming way.

fun.why: The prose was witty and exploring was easy.

engagement.why: It was a short session. The key hook was interesting, but I left early.

difficulty.why: Moving around and taking things was simple. The only snag was the dark tunnel.

interestingness.why: Illusions that the world itself comments on were a fresh idea.

prose.why: The wry narration of the illusions stood out.
